security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, inline filenames, zipfile usage, and validation text. No prompt injection, network access, credential exfiltration, or malicious command execution was found. Two medium semantic filesystem issues remain: unvalidated skill-name path construction and unfiltered recursive packaging.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated skill names can alter the generated output path.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce the documented hyphen-case name regex, reject path separators and absolute names, resolve the final destination, and verify it stays under the requested base directory.

remediation.issue: The packager archives every recursive file under the skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit allowlist or denylist for package contents, skip symlinks and VCS folders, and block common secret files such as .env, private keys, and certificates.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Can Escape Output Directory
semantic_findings.description: scripts/init_skill.py builds the destination from user-controlled path and skill_name without validating the skill name or resolving the final path under the requested base directory. A traversal-style skill name could create a new skill directory outside the intended output location.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script documents naming rules but passes argv values directly into path construction. The created files are fixed templates, so impact is filesystem write scope rather than arbitrary code execution.

semantic_findings.title: Packaging Recursively Includes All Skill Files
semantic_findings.description: scripts/package_skill.py archives every file returned by rglob without excluding hidden files, credentials, key material, version-control folders, or symlink targets. A skill package could unintentionally include local secrets or unrelated files placed inside the skill directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The recursive packaging loop is explicit and has no allowlist or denylist before zipf.write. The risk depends on local folder contents, so confidence is high for exposure potential but not proof of current secret leakage.

content.value_statement: Creating reusable AI skills is hard when structure, triggers, resources, and packaging rules are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a practical workflow for designing, scaffolding, validating, and packaging skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md frontmatter and instruction structure.
Guides selection of scripts, references, and assets for reusable workflows.
Provides an initializer that creates a template skill directory with example resources.
Provides a validator for basic frontmatter, naming, and description checks.
Provides a packager that validates a skill and creates a .skill archive.
References workflow and output-pattern guidance for richer skill design.
limitations: The generated template still requires manual editing and testing.
The validator checks basic structure, not complete marketplace policy compliance.
The scripts perform local filesystem writes and should run only in trusted workspaces.
The skill does not publish, install, or review marketplace submissions automatically.

use_cases.title: Create a New Agent Skill
use_cases.description: Plan the skill trigger, SKILL.md body, reusable scripts, reference files, and assets before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Review a current skill for concise instructions, progressive disclosure, useful resources, and clear packaging steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Skill Package
use_cases.description: Validate frontmatter and create a distributable .skill archive after the skill content is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new skill idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill plan for this task: [task]. Ask only the essential questions, then recommend SKILL.md sections, scripts, references, and assets.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Create the initial directory and template content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me scaffold a skill named [skill-name] in [directory]. Use the initializer, then explain which generated example files I should keep or remove.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Skill Instructions
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing SKILL.md for clarity and triggering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill for trigger clarity, concise instructions, progressive disclosure, and resource organization. Suggest specific edits before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this completed skill, identify packaging risks, run the packaging workflow, and summarize any files that should be excluded before distribution.

output_examples.input: I want a skill that helps fill and verify PDF forms.
output_examples.output: A skill plan with a clear trigger description, a PDF form workflow, suggested scripts for analysis and filling, and reference files for field mappings.

output_examples.input: Review my existing data-analysis skill before I package it.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering trigger quality, unnecessary files, reusable resources, validation results, and packaging concerns.

output_examples.input: Package this finished skill for sharing.
output_examples.output: A validation summary, a packaging result, and a short list of files that should be checked before the archive is distributed.

best_practices: Start from concrete user examples before choosing scripts, references, or assets.
Keep SKILL.md concise and link only the reference files needed for each workflow.
Run representative script tests and validation before packaging a skill.
anti_patterns: Adding extra README, installation, or changelog files that the skill does not need.
Hiding trigger information in the body instead of the description field.
Shipping unused template directories or example files in the final package.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI skills with a clear SKILL.md file, reusable resources, validation steps, and packaging support.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete production skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It creates structure and guidance, but the final content, scripts, assets, and tests still require review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is described as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can a skill include scripts and assets?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance explains when to include scripts, reference documents, and assets for reusable workflows.

faq.question: Does it validate skills before packaging?
faq.answer: Yes. The included packaging script runs a basic validator before creating a .skill archive.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the scripts anywhere?
faq.answer: No. Run them in trusted workspaces and review output paths and package contents before distribution.
